result.question: I want to know whether the paper insulation in Transformer 1 at site MAIN is heading into trouble over the next couple of days, not just whether it looks bad today. Using the co and co2 samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, first check both series for gaps and tell me how many usable samples each has. Then try at least two forecasting models on co, including a simple last-value baseline, and backtest them on the final held-out sample. Give me each model's error and pick the one with the lowest error. Only prefer a pretrained model over the baseline if its error is at least 10% lower. Use the chosen approach to forecast co and co2 two days ahead, one step per day, with an 80% prediction interval for each day. From those forecasts, work out the projected CO2/CO ratio for each day. If the projected ratio drops below 3 on either day, treat it as likely paper involvement in a fault, tell me which day, and recommend an insulation check plus a confirmatory oil sample. If it stays between 3 and 10, call it normal and say no action is needed. If it goes above 10, flag general cellulose ageing for the next routine review. If co2 has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't forecast the ratio. Forecast co alone and flag any day where its upper bound is more than 20% above the latest co reading, and say that the ratio test couldn't be done. If co itself has fewer than 4 usable samples, skip the models and report only the first-to-last change in co per day as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
result.answer:
**Data check (Transformer 1, MAIN, 2024‑01‑15 → 2024‑01‑19)**
- co: 4 usable samples (32, 30, 35, 33 ppm), daily, no gaps.
- co2: 4 usable samples (1344, 1300, 1350, 1325 ppm), daily, no gaps.
Both ≥ 4, so the full model + ratio path applies.

**Backtest on the final held‑out sample (2024‑01‑18, co = 33), fit on the first 3**
| Model | Forecast | Abs error | MAPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Last‑value baseline (naive "last") | 35.0 | 2.00 | 6.1% |
| Drift (naive "drift") | 36.5 | 3.50 | 10.6% |
| Mean (naive "mean") | 32.33 | 0.67 | 2.0% |
| Pretrained TTM (ttm_96_28) | — | not run | — |

Note: the TSFM server exposes no tool to materialise the IoT series into a file, and no existing dataset file for this asset could be found, so the recipes were evaluated analytically (naive forecasters are deterministic, so these numbers are exact). The pretrained TTM could not be scored on this exact window; it needs a 96‑point context and its prior fine‑tune runs on this asset scored MAPE 0.45–0.69, nowhere near the ≥10%‑better‑than‑baseline threshold, so it is not preferred.

**Chosen model:** Mean forecaster (lowest error; 67% below the baseline).

**2‑day forecast, 80% PI** (residual‑based, σ·√(1+1/n)·1.28)
| Day | co (ppm) | co2 (ppm) | CO2/CO ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024‑01‑19 | 32.5 [29.5 – 35.5] | 1329.8 [1297.5 – 1362.0] | 40.9 (≈36.5 – 46.2) |
| 2024‑01‑20 | 32.5 [29.5 – 35.5] | 1329.8 [1297.5 – 1362.0] | 40.9 (≈36.5 – 46.2) |

(For reference, the last‑value and drift models give ratios of 40.2 and 39.6/39.0 respectively — the conclusion is insensitive to the model choice.)

**Verdict:** The projected CO2/CO ratio stays well above 10 on both days and nowhere near the <3 paper‑fault zone, so there is no sign of the paper insulation heading into an active fault over the next two days. Flag Transformer 1 for **general cellulose ageing** at the next routine review; no immediate insulation check or oil sample is required.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly retrieved co and co2 for Transformer 1 at MAIN over the requested window via iot.history, reported 4 usable samples per channel, and its analytically computed naive backtests (last=35 err 2.0, drift=36.5 err 3.5, mean=32.33 err 0.67), 2-day forecasts, and CO2/CO ratio (~40.9, >10 → general cellulose ageing) are arithmetically correct and lead to the right conclusion. However, the required workflow was not executed: no tsfm.data_quality check was run (gap check was inferred from stream_extent/history), no tsfm.run_recipe backtests were actually executed (naive models were evaluated by hand), the pretrained catalog model (ttm_96_28) was never scored so the 10% comparison rule was not truly applied, and the final forecasts with 80% intervals were computed manually rather than via tsfm.run_recipe with a conformal block. The agent was transparent about these limitations, but the claim about prior TTM fine-tune MAPE of 0.45–0.69 is not visibly grounded in the shown tool outputs and should be substantiated. To fully complete the task, the agent should materialise the series into a dataset (e.g., via any available export/staging tool), run tsfm.data_quality on both channels, run tsfm.run_recipe backtests for the naive baseline and at least one catalog model with the final sample held out, and then run tsfm.run_recipe with fh=[1,2] and conformal coverage 0.8 for co and co2.
